actor.description: Recorded actor identity, not host-authenticated authority.

file.description: A staged file relative to the work directory. The consumer verifies its actual bytes against sha256.

relativePath.description: A slash-separated file path relative to the work directory; no absolute path, dot segment, parent traversal, drive prefix or backslash.

context.description: Supporting notes and reference files used to understand the task, separate from its inputs. Empty collections explicitly mean no extra context. Context does not grant additional execution authority.
context.title: Request context

decision.description: .works/<workId>/decisions/<id>.json: an attributed decision on an exact work revision and subject digest. Identity and authority are not authenticated by this schema.
decision.title: Decision

evidence.description: .works/<workId>/evidence/<id>.json: artifact metadata. Existence, actual digest and evidentiary relevance require separate checks.
evidence.title: Evidence

index.description: Version 1 of the proposed .works document format. A document must match exactly one kind. This contract does not migrate or reinterpret legacy session records.
index.title: Works document contract

inputs.description: The prompts and files the request asks the skill to act on. At least one prompt or file is required.
inputs.title: Request inputs

output.description: One produced output. Text is inline; commits identify a repository and full object ID; images and other files bind persisted artifacts. Output metadata alone does not prove correctness or publication.
output.title: Response output

request.description: .works/<workId>/requests/<id>.json: prompts and files to act on, with supporting context kept separate, against one work revision. This record alone grants no execution permission.
request.title: Request

response.description: .works/<workId>/responses/<id>.json: typed outputs produced for one request. Optional verification observations describe their checks separately; delivering an output is not a claim that the work is proved complete.

feedbackRound.description: Completed feedback-and-repair rounds for this request. Initial candidate is round zero; the caller maintains truthful history.

response.title: Response

work.description: .works/<id>/work.json: goal, declared scope, acceptance criteria and current lifecycle.
work.title: Work

@cli/python.bind: Resolved executable path and reported version in the active environment; working directory and arguments declared by the invocation.
@cli/python.note: Resolve Python 3 from the active environment: python, python3, or py -3 as appropriate; record the selected executable and any launcher arguments.

@tools/fileread.bind: Capability advertised by the active session; availability and invocation permissions checked at use time.
@tools/fileread.purpose: Read declared workspace files and directories through the active session.

claude.via: Claude Code Read, Glob and Grep

@tools/imagegen.bind: Capability advertised by the active session; availability and invocation permissions checked at use time.
@tools/imagegen.purpose: Produce artwork: a digital image from an image model, made to one stated claim. Rendering HTML is the visualize tool, not this one.

claude.via: none; a judged step records that no artwork could be made and the branch continues; a required step blocks with the operator's own code

openai.via: the OpenAI image model available to the Codex session

@tools/imageview.bind: Image inspection capability advertised by the active session; inspect actual pixels, not filenames or metadata.
@tools/imageview.purpose: Inspect image pixels through session image input or an image viewing tool.

claude.via: Attached images or an image-capable file reader.

openai.via: Attached images or an available image viewing tool.

@tools/print.bind: Capability advertised by the active session; availability and invocation permissions checked at use time.
@tools/print.purpose: Present text and artifacts in the conversation using the host rendering capabilities.

claude.via: the session's file and render hand-off, which displays an image or an HTML page in the conversation and falls back to the path or the URL

openai.via: the absolute path or the URL printed into the conversation, with the image inline where the client renders one

@tools/sourcewrite.bind: Capability advertised by the active session; availability and invocation permissions checked at use time.
@tools/sourcewrite.purpose: Edit files within the declared write scope through the active session.

@workspaces/artifacts.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/artifacts.purpose: Produced files, including images, documents and other deliverables.

@workspaces/context.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/context.purpose: Supporting reference files for a request.

@workspaces/fe.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/fe.purpose: The explicitly bound frontend checkout; unavailable when the project has no frontend role.

@workspaces/grammar.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/grammar.purpose: The explicitly resolved grammar package directory; unavailable when no grammar package is bound.

@workspaces/inputs.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/inputs.purpose: Files supplied as the subject of a request.

@workspaces/knowledge.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/knowledge.purpose: Knowledge published by the selected skill runtime.

@workspaces/requests.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/requests.purpose: Requests with separate inputs and context.

@workspaces/responses.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/responses.purpose: Responses declaring produced outputs and execution status.

@workspaces/work.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/work.purpose: One work record and its associated files.

criteria.history: The caller records the initial candidate at feedbackRound 0 and increments once per repair round. Keep concise failed-criterion feedback, submitted prompts, prior response ids, and accepted outputs. Delete rejected generated images and adjacent previews; remove their output references from mismatch responses. Never delete supplied baselines. Bind every response to the original request and work revision. Only a passing replacement is presented and copied beside its response JSON.

onFail.instruction: Ask for the missing fact that materially determines the design. Do not redraw to guess business facts or fabricate source evidence.

onFail.instruction: Confirm the previous call failed before retrying. If completion is uncertain, inspect its status first to avoid duplicate generation. Retry only within the feedback-round budget; do not automatically retry quota, policy or permission refusals.

criteria.stopWhen: Stop after two feedback rounds, when the same failure recurs after correction, when capability is blocked, or when essential inputs must change. Return mismatch for an unacceptable produced direction, blocked for an execution failure, or waiting for missing input. Never return done with failed or unchecked criteria. A retry is not proof of acceptance.

purpose: Draw one interface direction as a PNG from the supplied brief and references, inspect it, and present it with the exact generation prompt and design rationale.

request.description: Use the shared request envelope. inputs.prompts and inputs.files contain the drawing task and source material; context.notes and context.files contain supporting references. expected records the acceptance criteria. Resolve missing essential details before generation; do not invent product claims or facts.
request.title: interface.draw request

response.description: A done response contains the direction PNG, exact prompt file and inline rationale. Additional assets or review files may be included. Non-done responses explain their reason and may retain partial outputs.
response.title: interface.draw response

scope: Design artifact only. The request supplies the surface, audience, content, actions and constraints. Existing frontend, grammar and knowledge are optional references when explicitly bound. Implementation is a separate operation.

calls.purpose: Read the request and only its declared file references.

steps.instruction: Read the exact request and declared files. Separate task inputs from context. Establish surface, audience, content, primary actions and visual constraints. Ask only for essential missing information; record reasonable assumptions. Select context.visual mode explicitly. For an existing surface or feature extension, bind its current or selected image as baseline in context.files. Do not choose new just to bypass missing context.
produces: An understood brief with known facts, constraints and explicit assumptions.

steps.instruction: Read relevant bound references. Write the complete generation prompt: surface and viewport intent, hierarchy, exact supplied content, actions, visual language and reference usage. Preserve native-control and live-data intent; a drawing is not an implemented screen. State visual.preserve and visual.change explicitly; identify which regions remain intact. For extend/revise, append every preserve/change item verbatim as a checklist in the retained prompt; additional design explanation may follow.

steps.instruction: Submit the retained prompt and declared reference images to image generation. Produce one interface PNG and persist the actual returned result. If the host returns inaccessible media, explain the persistence limit rather than inventing a local path. Pass the actual baseline image to the image-edit/generation call for extend/revise; mentioning a path in text is insufficient. The model does not supply durable image memory. Retain generation-context with requestId, attemptId, mode and the exact baseline, prompt and result file bindings.

steps.instruction: Write the response with actual paths, media types and SHA-256 digests. Run request and response machine checks. Present the PNG inline followed by rationale and prompt reference. Report incomplete checks truthfully; claim neither user approval nor working frontend behavior. Evaluate every review criterion against actual pixels and record its criterionId, result, referenced outputIds and concrete note in criteriaResults. Cover every request expected id with a passed observation before done. Follow criteria.json on failure, increment feedbackRound after each repair, and reassess all affected checks. Delete rejected generated images and preview copies after recording defects; retain only accepted images as response outputs and adjacent previews. Do not present an unaccepted direction.

validate.failurePolicy: Use recovery.json to select the repair, limits, history and stop status. Machine validation never establishes visual acceptance.
